roadmap_item: §5 item 7e, M2d: the bridge stage re-run with the joint fit on the pinned CRISPRi pairs
question: M1c (signaltrace) followed the held-out ENCODE CRISPRi pairs in K562 through the compiled layer and lost the measured signal at the bridge: target choice kept 39 of 1,918 pairs with a gain over activity and distance (+0.0792 [95% CI 0.0282, 0.1562]), and the bridge in K562 kept none, because every gene those pairs reach carries two or more compiled rules, which bridge.parameterize cannot identify. With the bridge replaced by combine2's joint fit of a gene's elements - once under the runtime's mean, once under the promoter-competition form, each as combine2 committed it - and the reader gate, the regulator assignment and the run following it as in M1c, does the agreement with the measured CRISPRi outcome survive the bridge once the genes are fittable?
population: signaltrace's population, reused and not re-chosen: the 1,918 K562 pairs of the ENCODE held-out file, each identified as chrom:chromStart-chromEnd:measuredGeneSymbol, in file order, whose newline-joined list has the sha256 signaltrace's registration (data/results/signaltrace_registration.json) pins; the run refuses if the pairs it reads differ from that list. The label is the file's Regulated column, the anchor's own. Every stage is read on all 1,918: a pair a stage drops stays with 0 in that stage's two columns. The fit rows are the anchor's and signaltrace's: the K562 training pairs crispri.annotate marks covered, unchanged for every stage
predicted_only: every stage after the anchor reads the compiled programs with their experimental rule lines removed. Those rules carry the CRISPRi screens' own EffectSize, the held-out file's pairs included (marked 'held-out split, evaluation only, never a feature'), and the bridge prefers an experimental rule to a predicted one for the same mechanism (bridge.PRECEDENCE), so a stage that read them would read the outcome. The removed lines are counted per program and must equal readergate.rule_targets' count of experimental rule lines; nothing else in a program is changed

fit.principle: the bridge's: the run reproduces each element's own removal observation RHO_i = 2**(log2 fold change on deletion) exactly at the state where every element of the gene is present (S5, 'direction and fold ... are the input'), and the gene's intact transcription is its rate T (measured, else the borrowed median; no fold prediction depends on T)
fit.mean: d_i = 1 - RHO_i (activating), e_j = RHO_j - 1 (inhibiting). q = sum d_i is the element-driven share of intact transcription, basal b = T(1 - q); an inhibitor's s_j*h = e_j/(q + e_j); an activator's s_i = d_i/max d (DECLARED_STRENGTH convention: the strongest has s = 1) with max_rate V = n * max d * T / (h * R0). Level relative to T with the open set O: (1 - q) + [sum of d_i over open activators] * prod over closed inhibitors (1 + e_j/q)
fit.competition: K = THETA/(1 - THETA); weights kappa_i (sum K) and Z = V*R0/T solve d_i = Z*kappa_i/((1 + K)(1 + K - kappa_i)), i.e. sum over i of d_i(1 + K)^2/(Z + d_i(1 + K)) = K, one root Z > 0 (brentq). q = Z*THETA, b = T(1 - q), s_j*h = e_j/(q + e_j); s_i = kappa_i/max kappa and the gene's promoter_half_saturation = h/max kappa (DECLARED_STRENGTH convention). Level relative to T: (1 - q) + Z * W/(1 + W) * prod over closed inhibitors (1 + e_j/q), W the sum of kappa_i over open activators
fit.runnable: a gene is runnable under a form when the fit gives b > 0 (q < 1) and every fitted s in (0, 1] (bridge.STRENGTH_TOLERANCE above 1 allowed); otherwise it is reported by reason and not run

form_sources.mean: runtime/grn.py's default since the first commit (ACTIVATOR_COMBINATION = 'mean'), as the runtime runs it with the reader: A = (1/n) * sum of s_i*H(x_i) over the gene's n activating rules, a held rule counted at strength 0; inhibitors multiply, R = prod (1 - s_j*H(x_j)). Under the hold the mean is linear in the element terms: closing elements adds their contributions
form_sources.competition: grn OPT_IN_ACTIVATOR_RULES 'competition': A = W/(K + W), W = sum of s_i*H(x_i). Source: Bothma JP, Garcia HG, Ng S, Perry MW, Gregor T, Levine M (2015) Enhancer additivity and non-additivity are determined by enhancer strength in the Drosophila embryo. eLife 4:e07956, doi 10.7554/eLife.07956, PMC4532966, Methods 'Mathematical modeling' eqs. 7-9 (a promoter engaged by at most one enhancer at a time; read here for n enhancers). Declared, not from the paper: one transcriptional efficiency r for every element of a gene (the paper's eq. 9 lets each have its own; with one r the form is monotone and cannot give snail's pair below its stronger single); the promoter occupancy THETA = 0.5 with every element present; and the runtime's basal rate, which the paper's model does not have. Inhibitors multiply, as under the mean

form_words.competition: the promoter-competition form (Bothma 2015, declared half-occupied promoter)

joint_fit: per chromosome, the program with its experimental rule lines removed (PREDICTED_ONLY) is gated as signaltrace's s4_bridge gated it (compile.gate_program, selection reader_cells: every predicted rule is offered in K562 whatever its compiled cell) and parsed. Every gene that a rule reached by the traced pairs (fit rows and population, signaltrace.chromosome_lookup's reached rules) targets is read by combine2.gene_rules on that module: all of the gene's rules in that program, each with its removal observation (bridge.observation_of) and its reader states. combine2.classify admits it (every observation readable, none exactly 1, each rule's action agreeing with its observation's sign, at least one activating) and combine2.fit gives each form's joint fit; a gene is runnable under a form as combine2.FIT['runnable'] states. The rate T is the gene's rate in data/results/gene_rates.json, else that table's genome median (the borrowed tier, as combine2's census and signaltrace's bridge read it); no fold depends on T. A runnable gene is run by combine2.run_gene_form (its thirteen gated reader cells and its single-removal reproduction, combine2.HARNESS) and, in K562, once more for each of its elements open there with that element clamped absent (bridge.REMOVED), which under both forms equals holding the rule. The joint fit applies to a gene of any rule count; signaltrace found every one of the 377 reached rules not_identifiable in K562, so every gene read here has two or more

s1_anchor.name: the deletion feature (anchor)
s1_anchor.kept: crispri top_target: the measured gene is the single top predicted target of a deleted element overlapping the CRISPRi element, in the compact all-element table
s1_anchor.value: crispri deletion_drop: the largest predicted fall of the measured gene on deleting an overlapping element, on K562's own track, from the per-element cache (any gene the sweep scored)

s2_target.name: target choice
s2_target.kept: an element of the compiled programme that overlaps the CRISPRi element (half-open intervals) carries a predicted rule whose target gene's symbol is the measured gene
s2_target.value: the anchor's deletion_drop, on kept pairs only, so this stage changes only which pairs are kept

s3_compiled_value.name: the value the compiled rule states
s3_compiled_value.value: the compiled rule's own strength (|log2 fold change| in its compiled cell, the argmax track over the scorer's RNA-seq tracks, clipped at 1) for an activating rule and 0 for an inhibiting one, the largest over the kept rules

s4_joint_mean.name: the strength combine2's joint fit gives in K562, the runtime's mean
s4_joint_mean.kept: a rule kept by s3_compiled_value (an overlapping element's predicted rule naming the measured gene) whose gene the joint fit makes runnable under mean (JOINT_FIT), the rule among the gene's fitted rules
s4_joint_mean.value: max(0, -log2 RHO) of the rule's removal observation, which the fitted run reproduces at the state where every element of the gene is present (combine2.HARNESS (2)); the largest over the kept rules. It is signaltrace's s4_bridge value, now carried for every rule of a fitted gene

s5_reader_mean.name: the reader gate in K562 after the joint fit, the runtime's mean
s5_reader_mean.kept: a rule kept by s4_joint_mean whose element the gated program's K562 reader block states open (an ENCODE DNase-seq narrowPeak overlaps it); closed and unknown hold the rule
s5_reader_mean.value: as s4_joint_mean, over the open rules

s6_regulator_mean.name: the regulator assignment in K562 after the joint fit, the runtime's mean
s6_regulator_mean.kept: a rule kept by s5_reader_mean whose element signaltrace's lookup gives a source factor in K562 (regulators.candidates with the rule's cell set to K562: an ENCODE TF ChIP-seq peak cluster naming K562 overlaps the element)

s7_run_mean.name: the jointly fitted run's predicted change in K562, the runtime's mean
s7_run_mean.kept: a rule kept by s5_reader_mean, run: the gene's fitted program (combine2.fitted_module on readergate.gated_gene_module) run by runtime.grn.NetworkRuntime with activator_combination=mean in K562, every element clamped present so that the reader holds the closed ones
s7_run_mean.value: max(0, log2(L_K562 / L_held)): the gene's level in K562 with the reader applied, over its level with this rule held as well (its element clamped absent); the largest over the run rules. The gene's other elements are open or held as K562's reader states them, so this is the rule's own observation only when no other element of the gene changes the level it acts on

s4_joint_competition.name: the strength combine2's joint fit gives in K562, the promoter-competition form (Bothma 2015, declared half-occupied promoter)
s4_joint_competition.kept: a rule kept by s3_compiled_value (an overlapping element's predicted rule naming the measured gene) whose gene the joint fit makes runnable under competition (JOINT_FIT), the rule among the gene's fitted rules
s4_joint_competition.value: max(0, -log2 RHO) of the rule's removal observation, which the fitted run reproduces at the state where every element of the gene is present (combine2.HARNESS (2)); the largest over the kept rules. It is signaltrace's s4_bridge value, now carried for every rule of a fitted gene

s5_reader_competition.name: the reader gate in K562 after the joint fit, the promoter-competition form (Bothma 2015, declared half-occupied promoter)
s5_reader_competition.kept: a rule kept by s4_joint_competition whose element the gated program's K562 reader block states open (an ENCODE DNase-seq narrowPeak overlaps it); closed and unknown hold the rule
s5_reader_competition.value: as s4_joint_competition, over the open rules

s6_regulator_competition.name: the regulator assignment in K562 after the joint fit, the promoter-competition form (Bothma 2015, declared half-occupied promoter)
s6_regulator_competition.kept: a rule kept by s5_reader_competition whose element signaltrace's lookup gives a source factor in K562 (regulators.candidates with the rule's cell set to K562: an ENCODE TF ChIP-seq peak cluster naming K562 overlaps the element)

s7_run_competition.name: the jointly fitted run's predicted change in K562, the promoter-competition form (Bothma 2015, declared half-occupied promoter)
s7_run_competition.kept: a rule kept by s5_reader_competition, run: the gene's fitted program (combine2.fitted_module on readergate.gated_gene_module) run by runtime.grn.NetworkRuntime with activator_combination=competition in K562, every element clamped present so that the reader holds the closed ones
s7_run_competition.value: max(0, log2(L_K562 / L_held)): the gene's level in K562 with the reader applied, over its level with this rule held as well (its element clamped absent); the largest over the run rules. The gene's other elements are open or held as K562's reader states them, so this is the rule's own observation only when no other element of the gene changes the level it acts on

anchor.model: activity + distance + deletion against activity + distance, weights fitted on the covered K562 training pairs (crispri.score_published), average precision, crispri.gain_interval

comparator: the anchor and signaltrace's s2_target and s3_compiled_value, recomputed by signaltrace's own code on the same pairs and fit rows; the run stops (HARNESS_DEFECT) unless the anchor equals its committed arm-1 figures and s2_target and s3_compiled_value equal signaltrace's committed readings exactly (data/results/signaltrace_result.json: kept counts, gain over activity and distance, interval, and against the anchor with its interval). Every joint stage is read against the anchor and against the stage it follows by the same paired resampling; signaltrace's s4_bridge reading (NONE_KEPT) and chain reading are quoted beside it, verbatim
metric: the anchor's metric, unchanged. A stage's model is activity + distance (log_distance, log_activity, activity_over_distance) plus the stage's two columns, kept (0 or 1) and value, both 0 for a pair the stage drops (the benchmark's minimum-score rule, as the anchor treats an uncovered pair); for the anchor the two columns are top_target and deletion_drop. Each model is fitted by crispri.logistic_fit (lam 1e-3, 25 rounds) on the fit rows and scored on the 1,918 population pairs; the score is average precision (crispri.average_precision). A stage's reading is its average precision minus the activity + distance model's (its gain), with the 95% interval of crispri.gain_interval (2,000 resamples of whole chromosomes, seed 0); beside it, by the same paired resampling, the stage minus the anchor and the stage minus the stage it follows

bootstrap.unit: chromosome: whole chromosomes resampled with replacement, the anchor's unit

decision: per stage after the anchor, with [lo, hi] the 95% interval of its gain over activity + distance and [dlo, dhi] that of its average precision minus the anchor's: NONE_KEPT if the stage keeps none of the 1,918 pairs; else WORSE if hi < 0; WEAKENED if lo > 0 and dhi < 0; CARRIES if lo > 0; LOST if dhi < 0; otherwise UNDECIDED. The chain (s2_target, s3_compiled_value, s4_bridge, s5_reader, s7_run) is walked in order and stops at the first stage whose outcome is neither CARRIES nor WEAKENED: LOST_AT that stage if its outcome is NONE_KEPT, LOST or WORSE, UNDECIDED_AT it if UNDECIDED. If no stage stops it: WEAKENED_NOT_LOST if any chain stage is WEAKENED, else CARRIED_TO_THE_RUN. 'Loses the signal' means exactly this: the stage's interval of gain over activity and distance no longer lies above zero, and its interval against the anchor lies below zero. No margin beyond the intervals is applied
per_form: signaltrace's DECISION is applied to each form F on its own chain (s2_target, s3_compiled_value, s4_joint_F, s5_reader_F, s7_run_F), with s4_joint_F in s4_bridge's place, s5_reader_F in s5_reader's and s7_run_F in s7_run's, and s6_regulator_F read beside it on s5_reader_F's pairs as signaltrace reads s6_regulator. The two forms are read separately, each at the anchor's 95% interval; neither reading is pooled with the other, and no difference between the forms is tested
bridge_decision: per form, from s4_joint_F's outcome under DECISION: SURVIVES if CARRIES or WEAKENED (the 95% interval of its gain over activity and distance lies above zero, so the chain passes the bridge), LOST if NONE_KEPT, LOST or WORSE (signaltrace's LOSS), UNDECIDED if UNDECIDED. 'Survives' means exactly that; whether the gain is below the anchor's is the stage reading's own clause, kept beside it
stop_rule: one run, from this registration's committed code, on the cached files the registration pins by sha256, signaltrace's and combine2's registrations among them. No stage, column, population, fit row, form, parameter, metric or wording is changed after any joint stage is read; a defect found afterwards is reported beside the registered readings and corrected only under a new registration. The run stops with HARNESS_DEFECT, before any joint stage is read, if: the population differs from signaltrace's pinned list; a field of combine2's registration in COMBINE2_BOUND differs from combine2.py; signaltrace's own stage columns, recomputed, differ on any population pair from its committed pairs table; signaltrace's own harness fails; a reached gene is not read from the gated program, or its K562 reader state differs from signaltrace's lookup; any gene-form run misses combine2.HARNESS or a K562 run with one more element held differs from the form's closed form by more than CLOSED_FORM_TOLERANCE in log2; a joint stage keeps a pair the stage it follows dropped; the anchor does not reproduce the committed arm-1 figures; or s2_target or s3_compiled_value does not reproduce signaltrace's committed reading

outcomes.HARNESS_DEFECT: stopped before any stage beyond the anchor was read: {what}
outcomes.ANCHOR: anchor reproduced: the deletion feature's gain over activity and distance is {g} [95% CI {lo}, {hi}] on the {n} held-out K562 pairs ({k} with the measured gene as an overlapping element's top predicted target, {kp} of them regulated), as committed
outcomes.NONE_KEPT: none kept: the stage keeps none of the {n} held-out K562 pairs ({kf} of the {nf} fit rows), so no compiled prediction reaches the measurement at this stage; gain over activity and distance {g} [95% CI {lo}, {hi}], against the anchor {d} [95% CI {dlo}, {dhi}]
outcomes.CARRIES: carries the anchor's signal: gain over activity and distance {g} [95% CI {lo}, {hi}] on the {n} held-out K562 pairs ({k} kept by the stage, {kp} of them regulated); against the anchor {d} [95% CI {dlo}, {dhi}], no difference detected
outcomes.WEAKENED: weakened: a gain over activity and distance remains, {g} [95% CI {lo}, {hi}] on the {n} held-out K562 pairs ({k} kept by the stage, {kp} of them regulated), and it is below the anchor's, {d} [95% CI {dlo}, {dhi}]
outcomes.LOST: lost: no gain over activity and distance detected, {g} [95% CI {lo}, {hi}] on the {n} held-out K562 pairs ({k} kept by the stage, {kp} of them regulated), and below the anchor, {d} [95% CI {dlo}, {dhi}]
outcomes.UNDECIDED: undecided: no gain over activity and distance detected, {g} [95% CI {lo}, {hi}] on the {n} held-out K562 pairs ({k} kept by the stage, {kp} of them regulated), and no difference from the anchor detected either, {d} [95% CI {dlo}, {dhi}]
outcomes.WORSE: worse: below activity and distance alone, {g} [95% CI {lo}, {hi}] on the {n} held-out K562 pairs ({k} kept by the stage, {kp} of them regulated); against the anchor {d} [95% CI {dlo}, {dhi}]

chain_outcomes.LOST_AT: the measured signal is lost at {stage} ({name}): {stage_reading}{before}
chain_outcomes.UNDECIDED_AT: the chain cannot say where the signal goes from {stage} ({name}) on: {stage_reading}{before}
chain_outcomes.WEAKENED_NOT_LOST: the measured signal is weakened, first at {stage} ({name}), and not lost before the run: at the run, {run_reading}
chain_outcomes.CARRIED_TO_THE_RUN: the measured signal is carried through every stage to the run: at the run, {run_reading}

bridge_outcomes.SURVIVES: with the genes fitted jointly under {form}, the measured signal survives the bridge: at {stage} ({name}), {stage_reading}
bridge_outcomes.LOST: with the genes fitted jointly under {form}, the measured signal does not survive the bridge: at {stage} ({name}), {stage_reading}
bridge_outcomes.UNDECIDED: with the genes fitted jointly under {form}, whether the measured signal survives the bridge is not decided: at {stage} ({name}), {stage_reading}

limitations: the metric ranks all 1,918 pairs; a stage that keeps few of them can move the ranking of those few only, so a loss at such a stage says that the stage's predictions reach too few of the measured pairs, as much as anything about the values it carries. The kept counts stand beside every reading for that reason

a K562 reader state is ENCODE DNase-seq peak overlap and a regulator is ENCODE TF ChIP-seq occupancy: accessibility and occupancy, not function. AlphaGenome was trained on ENCODE, so neither is independent of the deletion feature

the held-out file's positives were filtered on chromatin at the tested element (crispri.POSITIVE_FILTER, found post hoc on 2026-09-27) and the activity column reads H3K27ac from the same file; every stage shares that baseline, so it cancels from the stage-to-stage comparisons and not from a gain over activity and distance
the bridge's rates are mouse NIH 3T3 or their genome median; the predicted change does not depend on them (runrules.READING), and no level in molecules per cell is quoted
no stage is a test of a mechanism: a stage that carries the signal says only that the compiled layer, at that stage, still ranks the measured pairs better than activity and distance do

the joint fit treats a gene's k observations as taken at one intact state, but each is the argmax over 371 tracks in its own track, and each reader cell's run transports them there. A maximum per element inflates the summed single-removal effects, which is one reason most multi-element genes are not runnable under either form (the census)

the population is the genes whose summed single-removal effects leave a positive basal rate under the form: a selected subset of the multi-element genes, different for each form; a gene that is not runnable is not run, and nothing here says how those genes would read

declared, not measured: the competition form's promoter occupancy THETA = 0.5 and one transcriptional efficiency per gene; the DECLARED_STRENGTH convention fixing the scale of s; the bridge's Hill assumptions (K = 1, n = 2, h = 0.5), which decide which inhibitors are feasible (s <= 1)

a pair whose gene no form can fit is dropped at s4_joint with 0 in the stage's two columns, as the anchor treats an uncovered pair; the runnable genes are those whose summed single-removal effects leave a positive basal rate, a selected subset that differs between the forms

at s4_joint the value is the rule's own observation under both forms, because each fit reproduces every single-removal observation; s4_joint_mean and s4_joint_competition differ only in the pairs they keep. The forms differ in value only at s7_run, where the gene's other elements are open or held as K562's reader states them
two forms are read, each at the anchor's 95% interval with no adjustment for reading two; each form's reading stands alone, nothing here pools them, and no difference between the forms is tested
this lane read signaltrace's committed readings and combine2's census and result before registering (exploration_preceded_this): the comparators are known, the joint stages on the real pairs are not
descriptives_not_verdicts: per form: the reached genes by whether the joint fit runs them and, where not, why (combine2's reasons); the quantiles of q, the element-driven share of intact transcription, over the reached runnable genes

per stage: the pairs kept of the 1,918 and of the fit rows, how many of them regulated, how many with a value above 0, the reasons the pairs it drops were dropped, the fitted weights of its model, and its paired interval against the stage it follows
the run checks: gene-form runs, K562 hold runs, the largest difference from the closed form in log2
signaltrace's committed s4_bridge and chain readings, quoted verbatim for context

anchor.model: activity + distance + deletion against activity + distance, weights fitted on the covered K562 training pairs (crispri.score_published), average precision, crispri.gain_interval

comparator_committed_verbatim.s2_target: weakened: a gain over activity and distance remains, +0.0792 [95% CI +0.0282, +0.1562] on the 1,918 held-out K562 pairs (39 kept by the stage, 35 of them regulated), and it is below the anchor's, -0.0569 [95% CI -0.0970, -0.0248]
comparator_committed_verbatim.s3_compiled_value: weakened: a gain over activity and distance remains, +0.0704 [95% CI +0.0225, +0.1412] on the 1,918 held-out K562 pairs (39 kept by the stage, 35 of them regulated), and it is below the anchor's, -0.0657 [95% CI -0.1109, -0.0297]
comparator_committed_verbatim.s4_bridge: none kept: the stage keeps none of the 1,918 held-out K562 pairs (0 of the 9,237 fit rows), so no compiled prediction reaches the measurement at this stage; gain over activity and distance +0.0000 [95% CI +0.0000, +0.0000], against the anchor -0.1361 [95% CI -0.2255, -0.0745]
comparator_committed_verbatim.chain_reading: the measured signal is lost at s4_bridge (the strength the bridge fits in K562): none kept: the stage keeps none of the 1,918 held-out K562 pairs (0 of the 9,237 fit rows), so no compiled prediction reaches the measurement at this stage; gain over activity and distance +0.0000 [95% CI +0.0000, +0.0000], against the anchor -0.1361 [95% CI -0.2255, -0.0745]; it was first weakened at s2_target (target choice)

exploration_preceded_this: stated so that nothing here is read as blind to figures this lane had seen. Before writing it the lane read: signaltrace's module, scripts and committed result (every stage's kept counts of the 1,918 pairs and the 9,237 fit rows, gains, intervals, outcomes and drop reasons: s2_target 39 kept, 35 regulated, +0.0792 [0.0282, 0.1562], WEAKENED; s3_compiled_value +0.0704 [0.0225, 0.1412], WEAKENED; s4_bridge NONE_KEPT, all 39 not_identifiable and all 377 reached rules not_identifiable; s4a 6 kept, +0.0260 [0.0027, 0.0711]; chain LOST_AT s4_bridge); combine2's module, census script and run script, its census (17,983 multi-element genes eligible for a fit; runnable 4,937 under the mean and 2,687 under competition, the rest mostly basal_not_positive; median summed single-removal drop 1.85; no gene with rules in several programs) and its registered RNA reading (both forms worse than the no-rule baseline). Which of the reached genes the joint fit makes runnable was NOT looked at: no joint stage was computed on any real pair before this file was committed; the joint stages were exercised only on the synthetic program of tests/test_s4joint.py
departures: s4a_bridge_as_compiled is not re-run: the brief names s4 and the chain after it; signaltrace's s4a reading stands as committed

combine2's POPULATION (a) asks that every rule of a gene be predicted; here the program is read with its experimental rule lines removed (signaltrace's PREDICTED_ONLY), so a gene whose program also carries a CRISPRi line is fitted on its predicted rules. Excluding it instead would select pairs by the CRISPRi screens' own layer, the held-out file included

combine2's POPULATION (e) (a prediction that varies across the thirteen cells) and (f) (an RNA row) are not applied: no RNA is read and the stages are read in K562 only; combine2's 13-cell runs are kept as the HARNESS, not as a filter
the joint fit is applied whatever a gene's rule count; combine2 ran genes with two or more rules, and signaltrace's committed result shows every reached rule's gene has two or more
the comparators are recomputed by signaltrace's own code and must reproduce its committed readings exactly, so the joint stages are read on the same footing as M1c's

frozen_code.tests: tests/test_s4joint.py (synthetic programs; not on the run's path, not pinned)

money: none: no request is sent and no key is read
network: none: every input is already on this machine

inputs.role: fit rows: the covered K562 training pairs
the population: its K562 pairs, scored

bootstrap.unit: chromosome: whole chromosomes resampled with replacement, the anchor's unit

parameters.selection: compile.SELECTION_READER_CELLS on the predicted-only program, as signaltrace's s4

exclusions: every stage after the anchor reads the compiled programs with their experimental rule lines removed. Those rules carry the CRISPRi screens' own EffectSize, the held-out file's pairs included (marked 'held-out split, evaluation only, never a feature'), and the bridge prefers an experimental rule to a predicted one for the same mechanism (bridge.PRECEDENCE), so a stage that read them would read the outcome. The removed lines are counted per program and must equal readergate.rule_targets' count of experimental rule lines; nothing else in a program is changed

a pair a stage drops is kept in the population with 0 in that stage's two columns
a gene combine2.classify excludes or a form's fit leaves not runnable: its pairs are dropped at s4_joint for that form

entry_script.why: argv[0] is a file inside this repository that git tracks and reports unmodified: the commit holds the code that wrote the bytes, so a rebuild can run it. The only clean form
entry_script.forms_are_decided_in_advance: genomeos.manifest.ENTRY_FORMS: one clean form (a tracked, unmodified file inside this repository), every other form refuses, and a form that cannot be classified is 'unknown' and refuses too. Read from sys.argv[0] at write time, never declared

code_cleanliness.counting_path_is_computed: the transitive import closure of this script, computed from the files' import statements at write time (genomeos.manifest.counting_path), never by importing: it follows every import that resolves to a file in this repository rather than only the package, counts the __init__.py of each package above a module, resolves bare imports against the directories the source literally puts on sys.path as well as the repository root, and matches every path component against what its directory lists, so a class name such as genomeos.genome.Genome cannot enter it as a file; not a hand-written list
code_cleanliness.note: several lanes work in this one checkout. A file under foreign_uncommitted_code belongs to another lane; this lane did not write it and did not commit it. The counting path is the computed closure above, so a foreign file outside it cannot have entered a number here, and foreign_uncommitted_code_on_the_counting_path names any that could

revision_stamps.sampled: code_cleanliness.git_sha is read while the writer computes; code.git_sha is read when the result is written. Both are HEAD of the same checkout at two moments
revision_stamps.reading: no revision race: both stamps record 9f199d6

traced_inputs.note: Every file this writer opened for reading under data/ was recorded by an audit hook on the "open" event, canonicalised through data/'s links so one file has one spelling, and compared against the inputs the manifest declares; a member of a declared group counts as declared and hashed on its own, a file under a declared directory counts as declared by prefix. The hook is per interpreter, so a file read by a subprocess is not in this record, nor is one reached through a path that canonicalises to neither this checkout's data/ nor one of its link targets.
